read.thesis: Grasberg Block Cave ramp cut: 2026 copper sales cut to 3.1bn lb from 3.4bn and PTFI output now ~65% of capacity in 2H26, while unit cash cost guide rose to $1.95/lb; supply stays impaired, not restored.

utilisation.quote: PTFI’s overall production rates, which were previously forecast to approximate 85% of capacity in the second half of 2026 and reach 100% of capacity by the end of 2027 are now expected to approximate 65% in the second half of 2026

capex.quote: Capital expenditures are expected to approximate $4.3 billion, including $3.0 billion for major mining projects, for the year 2026.

triggers.label: PTFI 2H26 rate 85% → 65%
triggers.quote: are now expected to approximate 65% in the second half of 2026

triggers.label: 2026 copper sales 3.4bn → 3.1bn lb
triggers.quote: Current sales estimates for the year 2026 are lower than January 2026 estimates of 3.4 billion pounds of copper

triggers.label: Q1 realised copper $5.78/lb
triggers.quote: Average realized prices were $5.78 per pound for copper

triggers.label: Bagdad expansion decision 2H26
triggers.quote: potential investment decision during the second half of 2026

guidance.quote: Consolidated sales are expected to approximate 3.1 billion pounds of copper
650 thousand ounces of gold and 90 million pounds of molybdenum for the year 2026
are expected to average $1.95 per pound of copper for the year 2026
operating cash flows are expected to approximate $8.7 billion
Capital expenditures are expected to approximate $4.3 billion
FCX is targeting annual production of approximately 300 million pounds of copper from these initiatives in 2026

prior_guidance_check.quote: which were favorable to the January 2026 estimate of $2.60 per pound

red_flags.label: Grasberg ramp slipped again
red_flags.quote: modifications to the chute system used to load ore into the automated trains will be required to operate at full capacity

red_flags.label: Energy/acid cost inflation from Middle East conflict
red_flags.quote: costs for certain petroleum-based energy products, sulfur and sulfuric acid, and other consumables have risen significantly
